items.title: Stage Two Opens: After Breakthrough, Two New Kinds of Obstacle

items.zh: 云何入聖諦現觀已，離諸障礙？當知此障略有二種。一、行處障，二、住處障。行處障者，謂如聖弟子，或與眾同居，隨其生起僧所作事，棄捨善品，數與眾會。或復安住常乞食法，而愛重飲食。或兼二處，好樂營為衣鉢等事。或為讀誦經典，而好樂談話。或居夜分，而樂著睡眠。或居晝分，樂王賊等雜染言論。或於是處，有親戚交遊談謔等住，而於是處不樂遠離。謂長夜數習與彼共居增上力故，或復樂與第二共住。諸如是等，名行處障。住處障者，謂處空閑修奢摩他、毘鉢舍那，總名為住。依奢摩他、毘鉢舍那，當知復有四種障礙。一、毘鉢舍那支不隨順性，二、奢摩他支不隨順性，三、彼俱品念不隨順性，四、處所不隨順性。
items.en: How, after entering the direct realisation of the noble truths, does one remove the obstacles? These obstacles should be known, in brief, as two kinds: obstacles of daily activity, and obstacles of formal practice. Obstacles of daily activity are these: a noble disciple dwelling among the community may be drawn into whatever monastic business arises, setting aside wholesome practice for frequent assemblies; may settle into constant almsround yet remain attached to food; may, in either setting, take pleasure in busying themselves with robes, bowls, and the like; may, while engaged in reading and reciting the scriptures, take pleasure in conversation; may, through the night, take pleasure in sleep; may, through the day, take pleasure in worldly talk of kings and bandits and the like; or may, in a place filled with relatives and companions and joking, find themselves unwilling to leave it. …Obstacles of formal practice are those that arise where one dwells in solitude cultivating calm-abiding and clear-seeing, called simply "dwelling." In reliance on calm-abiding and clear-seeing, four further obstacles should be known: an unfavorable disposition of the clear-seeing factor; an unfavorable disposition of the calm-abiding factor; an unfavorable disposition of the mindfulness shared by both; and an unfavorable disposition of the place itself.

items.zh: 若謂己聰明，而生高舉，不從他聞順觀正法，是名毘鉢舍那支不隨順性。若不安靜身語意行，躁動輕舉，數犯尸羅，生憂悔等，乃至不得心善安住，當知是名奢摩他支不隨順性。若有忘念增上力故，於沈掉等諸隨煩惱，心不遮護，當知是名彼俱品念不隨順性。若有習近五失相應諸坐臥具，當知是名處所不順隨性。或於晝分多諸諠逸；於夜分中多蚊虻等眾苦所觸；又多怖畏、多諸災厲；眾具匱乏，不可愛樂；惡友攝持，無諸善友。諸如是等，名住處障。

items.title: Two Remedies: Cultivating the Joy of Concentration

items.zh: 又此二障，當知總有二種因緣，能為遠離。一、多諸定樂，二、多諸思擇。多諸定樂，應知略有六種。謂若有已得三摩地，而未圓滿，未得自在；彼應修習止、舉、捨三種善巧，由此發生多諸定樂。
items.en: Regarding these two kinds of obstacle, two causes and conditions, in general, are capable of removing them: abundant joy in concentration, and abundant discernment. Abundant joy in concentration should be understood, in brief, to have six approaches. For one who has already attained concentration but not yet perfected or mastered it, one should cultivate the three skills of calming, uplifting, and equanimity, and thereby give rise to abundant joy in concentration.

items.title: The Remaining Marks of Concentration-Joy, and the Second Remedy: Discernment

items.zh: 若有於三摩地已得圓滿，亦得自在；彼應修習入、住、出定三種善巧，由此發生多諸定樂。云何名為多諸思擇？謂勝善慧，名為思擇。由此慧故，於晝夜分自己所有善法增長，如實了知；不善法增長，如實了知；善法衰退，如實了知；不善法衰退，如實了知。又彼如於晝夜若行、若住，習近衣服、飲食命緣。由習近故，不善法增長、善法衰退，或善法增長、不善法衰退，皆如實了知。即此思擇為依止故，於所生起諸不善法，由不堅著方便道理，驅擯遠離。於諸善法能勤修習。
items.en: For one whose concentration is already perfected and mastered, one should cultivate the three skills of entering, abiding in, and emerging from concentration, and thereby give rise to abundant joy in concentration. What is called abundant discernment? Excellent, superior wisdom is called discernment. Through this wisdom, day and night, one knows as it truly is whether one's own wholesome states are growing, whether unwholesome states are growing, whether wholesome states are declining, and whether unwholesome states are declining. Likewise, whether walking or standing, day or night, as one draws near to the conditions that sustain life — clothing, food — one knows as it truly is whether, through that drawing-near, unwholesome states grow while wholesome states decline, or wholesome states grow while unwholesome states decline. Resting on this discernment, whatever unwholesome states arise are driven out and set at a distance, through the method of not clinging to them; and the wholesome states are diligently cultivated.

items.title: Section: Stage Two Completes — Ten Skills Overcome Eleven Obstacles

items.zh: 如是二處十種善巧，於二處所十一種障，能令斷滅；隨所生起，即便遠離。如是名為遠離障礙。又此遠離障礙義，廣說應知如所說相。除此更無若過若增。
items.en: Thus these ten skills, belonging to the two domains, are able to dissolve the eleven obstacles belonging to those same two domains; whatever arises is immediately removed. This is called removing the obstacles. This meaning of removing the obstacles should, in full, be understood exactly as stated. Beyond this, there is nothing further to exceed it, and nothing further to add.

items.zh: 云何入聖諦現觀已，為欲證得速疾通慧，作意思惟諸歡喜事？

items.title: Section: Stage Three — Four Grounds for the Joy That Speeds Liberation

items.zh: 謂聖弟子，已見聖諦，已得證淨。即以證淨為依止故，於佛法僧勝功德田，作意思惟發生歡喜。又依自增上生事，及決定勝事，謂己身財寶所證盛事，作意思惟發生歡喜。又依無嫉，如於自身，於他亦爾。又依知恩，謂有恩者。念大師恩，作意思惟發生歡喜。由依彼故，遠離眾苦及與苦因，引發眾樂及與樂因。如是思惟隨順修道歡喜事故，便能證得速疾通慧。又此思惟隨順修道歡喜事義，廣說應知如所說相。除此更無若過若增。
items.en: A noble disciple who has already seen the noble truths has attained confirmed purity of faith. Resting on this confirmed purity, one applies the mind to the excellent field of merit that is the Buddha, the Dharma, and the saṅgha, and joy arises. Again, resting on one's own flourishing in higher rebirth and one's decisive excellence — the flourishing attained through one's own store of wealth [worldly and noble] — one applies the mind, and joy arises. Again, resting on freedom from envy, just as towards oneself, so too towards others. Again, resting on gratitude — recollecting the kindness of the Teacher — one applies the mind, and joy arises. In reliance on this, one grows distant from all manner of suffering and its cause, and draws forth all manner of happiness and its cause. Contemplating in this way the matters of joy that accord with the cultivation of the path, one is thereby able to attain swift, penetrating wisdom. This meaning of contemplating the matters of joy that accord with the cultivation of the path should, in full, be understood exactly as stated. Beyond this, there is nothing further to exceed it, and nothing further to add.

blocks.text: Even after stream-entry, there are obstacles. Today: what they are, the two remedies, and the four "matters of joy" that speed one towards liberation. One short passage is untranslated.

Obstacles after breakthrough are of two kinds: in **daily activity** and in **formal practice**. Venerable Miào Jìng: this concerns one who has already attained stream-entry, not a beginner. Daily obstacles include too much involvement in community business (Master Cháng Bǎi: "meetings", the monastic karman procedures), and delight in talk and even in recitation that crowds out practice.

Practice obstacles are four unfavourable conditions: for **insight**, the proud thinking oneself clever and not listening to others; for **calm**, restless conduct and remorse; for the **mindfulness** common to both, forgetfulness that lets dullness and agitation in; and an unsuitable **place**: noisy by day, full of mosquitoes at night, dangerous, lacking requisites, with bad friends and no good ones (untranslated, 0394a29).

**Abundant joy in concentration**: knowing when to calm, when to rouse, when to let be. Master Cháng Bǎi: when agitated, calm; when dull, rouse; when neither, equanimity. And **abundant discernment**: "excellent, superior wisdom", by which one knows day and night whether one's wholesome qualities are growing or declining. Ten skills overcome eleven obstacles.

Resting on confirmed purity of faith, one reflects with joy on four things: the Three Jewels as a field of merit (Master Cháng Bǎi: a field produces; merit planted there grows); one's own good rebirth and decisive excellence now assured; freedom from bad destinies; and the coming end of all suffering. This joy speeds liberation.

quiz.q: What two kinds of obstacle does the treatise say arise after entering direct realisation?
options: obstacles of daily activity and of formal practice
quiz.why: "These obstacles should be known, in brief, as two kinds: obstacles of daily activity, and obstacles of formal practice." Venerable Miào Jìng: this concerns those who have already attained stream-entry, not beginners.

quiz.q: At what level is the practitioner described by the obstacles of daily activity, per Venerable Miào Jìng?
options: one who has already attained stream-entry
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: this is not about one who has just aroused the aspiration; it is about one who has already attained stream-entry. The treatise likewise says "a noble disciple."

quiz.q: What four obstacles of formal practice arise in reliance on calm and insight?
options: the unfavorable disposition of the insight factor, the calm factor, the mindfulness shared by both, and the place
quiz.why: "An unfavorable disposition of the clear-seeing factor; of the calm-abiding factor; of the mindfulness shared by both; and of the place itself." Venerable Miào Jìng illustrates the first: "Why should I listen to you? I can understand just by reading."

quiz.q: What two causes and conditions does the treatise say remove these two obstacles?
options: abundant joy in concentration and abundant discernment
quiz.why: "Regarding these two kinds of obstacle, two causes and conditions, in general, are capable of removing them: abundant joy in concentration, and abundant discernment." Master Cháng Bǎi: the first is cultivating the power of calm, the second the excellent wisdom of insight.

quiz.q: When is each of calming, uplifting, and equanimity practised, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: calm when agitated, uplift when dull and drowsy, equanimity when neither and balanced
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: when the mind is agitated, practice calming; when dull and drowsy, uplifting; when neither dull nor restless and calm and uplift are balanced, practice equanimity.

quiz.q: How does the treatise define "abundant discernment"?
options: excellent wisdom, by which one knows day and night whether one's wholesome and unwholesome states are growing or declining
quiz.why: "Excellent, superior wisdom is called discernment. Through this wisdom, day and night, one knows as it truly is whether one's own wholesome states are growing." Master Cháng Bǎi: when unwholesome states decline, concentration grows; when they grow, concentration is lost.

quiz.q: On what four grounds does a noble disciple who has seen the truths apply the mind and give rise to joy?
options: the field of merit of the Three Jewels; one's own higher rebirth and decisive excellence; freedom from envy; gratitude, recollecting the Teacher's kindness
quiz.why: Resting on confirmed purity, one reflects on the Three Jewels as a field of merit; on one's own higher rebirth and decisive excellence; on freedom from envy; and on gratitude, recollecting the Teacher's kindness — and joy arises. Master Cháng Bǎi: the Three Jewels are called a "field" because a field produces.
